title: Media Call: Cyberattack Rumor — Confirm or Deny

transcript.speaker: Lena Torres
transcript.text: Hello, this is Lena Torres from Channel 5 News. I’m calling on behalf of our live report at noon. We’re getting multiple passenger calls saying the airport’s payment systems have been down for over an hour. One source says it was a cyberattack. Can you confirm or deny that?

transcript.speaker: Alex Morgan
transcript.text: Thank you for calling, Ms. Torres. We’re aware of the disruption to retail payment systems that began at approximately 9:47 AM. We’ve confirmed it was not a cyberattack. It was a configuration error in our network infrastructure.

transcript.speaker: Lena Torres
transcript.text: So you’re saying it was an internal mistake? Not a hack?

transcript.speaker: Alex Morgan
transcript.text: Yes. The issue was caused by a misapplied firewall rule that temporarily blocked all traffic to the Retail VLAN. The rule was corrected within 12 minutes. We are reviewing our change management procedures to prevent recurrence.

transcript.speaker: Lena Torres
transcript.text: And you’re confident no external threat was involved?

transcript.speaker: Alex Morgan
transcript.text: Absolutely. We have no evidence of unauthorized access or malicious activity. The block was unintentional, not an attack.

transcript.speaker: Lena Torres
transcript.text: Understood. We’ll include that in our on-air statement. Thanks for the clarity.

transcript.speaker: Alex Morgan
transcript.text: You’re welcome. We’re committed to transparency during this incident.
